checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add register fitting by octave displacement

impact_assessment.why: Transpose shifts all pitches by a fixed interval and invert mirrors them, but there is no way to fold stray notes into a target pitch range.
impact_assessment.benefits: register octave-displaces each sounding pitch into [low,high], preserving rhythm, velocity, pan and timbre as editable canonical source.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: bounds must be valid notes with low below high, rests untouched, out-of-range results skipped, and output must round-trip; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add byte-vector tests for octave folding, preservation and round-trip, a CLI command with --low/--high, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 289 tests green; octave folding, field preservation, round-trip and bound validation pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-register' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add a downward noise gate for WAVs

impact_assessment.why: trim only removes silence at file edges; there is no way to silence quiet frames between phrases of an existing WAV.
impact_assessment.benefits: gate silences frames below a dBFS threshold while leaving louder frames byte-identical, with exact frame and rate preservation.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: threshold must be a valid dBFS value, quiet frames zeroed, loud frames untouched, invalid WAVs rejected; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add byte-vector tests for threshold behaviour and identity, a CLI command reusing --threshold, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 294 tests green; selective gating, pass-through identity, all-frame gating and bounds pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-gate' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add deterministic bitcrush and decimation for WAVs

impact_assessment.why: bitdepth changes the container format and resample interpolates smoothly, but there is no lo-fi effect that reduces resolution and holds samples within a 16-bit WAV.
impact_assessment.benefits: crush quantizes samples to a chosen bit depth and repeats each sample for a hold factor, preserving frame count and sample rate with full-resolution identity.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: bits 1..16 and hold >=1, 16-bit/hold-1 identity exact, quantization grid exact, invalid WAVs and arguments rejected; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add byte-vector tests for identity, exact quantization grid and sample-and-hold, a CLI command with --crush-bits/--hold, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 299 tests green; full-resolution identity, quantization grid and sample-and-hold pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-crush' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: ad9a788defe5b66d45ad7b2f7b714dfa8a80f107

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add ring modulation for two WAVs

impact_assessment.why: mix overlays WAVs by addition but there is no way to multiply two signals, which is needed for amplitude modulation and simple lo-fi timbres.
impact_assessment.benefits: ring multiplies matching-rate Coda WAVs sample by sample, zero-pads the shorter input, and is an exact identity against full scale.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: rates must match, output uses the longer length, products clamp to range, identity must be byte-exact, invalid WAVs fail; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add byte-vector tests for product, identity, zero padding and rate validation, a CLI command taking two WAVs, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 304 tests green; per-channel products, identity, zero padding and rate validation pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-ring' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add an echo transform for existing WAVs

impact_assessment.why: Echo is available only as a render option, so a WAV that has been trimmed, crushed or mixed cannot receive a feedback delay.
impact_assessment.benefits: echo-to reuses the existing bounded comb echo on any Coda WAV, preserving frame count and rate, with zero delay byte-identical.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: invalid WAVs fail, zero delay is an identity, the delayed tail is exact and frames stay clamped; dependency: std only, reuse echo::apply_echo; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add byte-vector tests for impulse tail, identity and length preservation, a CLI command reusing --echo-delay/--echo-feedback, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 309 tests green; delayed tail, zero-delay identity, determinism and length preservation pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-echo-wav' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 03788fbbf41d4bc553ddf40f60f15bc98805d2c0

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add duration-only augmentation

impact_assessment.why: stretch scales both note starts and lengths, so there is no way to lengthen durations in place to create overlap or legato.
impact_assessment.benefits: augment multiplies only note durations by a factor, keeping starts, pitches and timbres fixed and producing canonical editable source.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: factor must be positive and finite, starts must be untouched, unit factor byte-identical, output must round-trip; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add byte-vector tests for duration scaling, start preservation and round-trip, a CLI command reusing --factor, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 314 tests green; duration-only scaling, start preservation and round-trip pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-augment' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add polarity inversion for WAVs

impact_assessment.why: The toolset can negate pitch (invert) and reverse audio (reverse-wav) but cannot flip sample polarity, a standard phase-cancellation utility.
impact_assessment.benefits: polarity negates every sample in place with exact double-application identity, preserving frame count and sample rate.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: sign of every sample must flip, applying twice must be byte-identical even at the i16 extreme, invalid WAVs must fail; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use wrapping i16 negation in the byte-vector module, add tests for sign flip, double identity and length, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 319 tests green; sign flips, byte-exact double inversion at i16 extreme and header preservation pinned by byte tests
